title: Spud Fling
pitch: Fling a googly-eyed potato, smash crates, unlock boosts, chase a new best.
description: Hold to charge a giant slingshot, release to fling Spud across a bright 3D field. Smash crate towers for potato coins, bounce off mushrooms, and climb an unlock ladder: Double Band, Bouncy Mushrooms, Air Toot, Pond of Gulpo, Mega Band, and Golden Spud. After the Gulpo unlock, a giant frog at the pond can swallow Spud and spit the potato out for a burst of distance. Single-player, one continuous progression mode. Progress saves locally in your browser.
howToPlay: Spud Fling is a one-button physics arcade game. Hold Space, Enter, mouse button, or touch to charge the slingshot (the power meter oscillates), then release to fling Spud. During flight, press again if you have unlocked Air Toot for a mid-air boost. After landing, press once more to reset and fling again. Smash crate towers for potato coins; unlocks happen automatically at coin thresholds. Single-player only — no accounts.
controls: Hold Space, Enter, mouse, or touch to charge; release to launch. During flight, press again for the unlocked Air Toot. After landing, press to reset.
controlsShort: One button: hold Space, Enter, mouse or touch to charge, release to fling
controlsKeyboard: Hold Space or Enter to charge; release to launch. Press again in flight for Air Toot (once unlocked). Press after landing to reset.
controlsTouch: Touch and hold anywhere to charge; release to launch. Tap again in flight for Air Toot (once unlocked). Tap after landing to reset.
tips: Release near the top of the charge oscillation for longer flights — the meter keeps moving while you hold.
Prioritize crate towers early; coins unlock Double Band and Bouncy Mushrooms that multiply later distance.
After Pond of Gulpo unlocks, aim flights over the pond near 95 m for the swallow-and-spit distance burst.
Golden Spud doubles coin gain — once you have it, farm crates to climb the remaining ladder faster.

howWeMade: We built it with AI assistance: AI coding agents wrote its code from our instructions. Spud Fling is one small JavaScript file on top of the open-source three.js engine (r149, MIT), drawn with WebGL1. Every mesh, colour and sound in it, from the potato and crates to the trees and the frog, is generated by our own code; the game ships no art, audio or font files. The physics is our own few lines of code rather than a physics library. We test it in headless Chromium with software WebGL (SwiftShader), with a fast-forward mode that speeds up coin gain so the unlocks can be checked; we have not measured it on real phones yet.

title: Pip's Bloom Isle
pitch: A cozy 3D platformer-collector: tend four island levels with Tansy while Pip cheers.
description: A cozy 3D platformer-collector for casual players 13+. Tansy, an original egg-shaped gardener, tends World 1 across four levels in order: Sunny Shelf, Stone Crossing, Islet Climb, and the Sulk Bulb. Pip the sprout follows and cheers when a level is cleared. Gentle, Breezy, and Bold change landing size and timing only. Art and audio are procedural. Progress, chosen tier, mute, and seen hints stay in localStorage on this device — no cookies, no account.
howToPlay: Play as Tansy, an original egg-shaped gardener, through World 1’s four levels in order: Sunny Shelf, Stone Crossing, Islet Climb, and the Sulk Bulb. Move, jump, dive, and plant to tend each island. Pip the sprout follows and cheers when you clear a level. Choose Gentle, Breezy, or Bold before you start — they only change landing size and timing. Audience: casual players 13+. Progress stays on this device in localStorage.
controls: Move with W A S D or arrow keys. Jump with 1 (or numpad 1); Space is a backup jump once a level is running. Dive with Shift or C. Plant with E. Pause with Esc. Start with Enter. Touch: left stick, jump and dive buttons, drag the right side to look.
controlsShort: W A S D or arrows to move, 1 to jump, Shift to dive, E to plant; touch stick and buttons
controlsKeyboard: Move: W A S D or arrows. Jump: 1 / numpad 1 (Space as backup once a level is running). Dive: Shift or C. Plant: E. Pause: Esc. Start: Enter.
controlsTouch: Left stick to move; on-screen jump and dive buttons; drag the right side of the screen to look.
tips: Clear levels in order — World 1 unlocks Sunny Shelf → Stone Crossing → Islet Climb → Sulk Bulb.
Try Gentle first if jumps feel tight; Breezy and Bold only change landing size and timing.
Plant with E when the prompt appears; Pip cheers when a level is cleared.

title: Merge Tiles
pitch: Gabriele Cirulli's open-source number puzzle (2048): slide tiles, merge pairs, aim for the 2048 tile.
description: Merge Tiles is our hosted copy of the open-source sliding-tile puzzle 2048 by Gabriele Cirulli et al., used under the MIT licence. Slide every tile with the arrow keys or a swipe; two tiles with the same number merge into one. The game logic is unchanged from the original. Best score and the current game stay in localStorage on its own web address; no cookies, no account.
howToPlay: The board is a 4×4 grid. Each move slides every tile as far as it can go in that direction, and a new 2 or 4 appears in an empty cell. When two tiles with the same number collide they merge into one tile with their sum. Keep merging to build bigger numbers and try to make the 2048 tile; you can keep going after that. The game ends when the board is full and no move can merge anything. New Game starts over; your best score is kept.
controls: Arrow keys to slide the tiles (W A S D and H J K L also work). Touch: swipe up, down, left or right on the board. New Game button restarts.
controlsShort: Arrow keys (or W A S D) or swipe to slide the tiles
controlsKeyboard: Arrow keys slide all tiles; W A S D or H J K L also work. Click New Game (or Try again) to restart.
controlsTouch: Swipe up, down, left or right on the board to slide the tiles. Tap New Game to restart.
tips: Pick a corner and keep your biggest tile in it.
Favour two directions (for example down and left) and use a third only when you must.
Avoid the move that pulls your biggest tile out of its corner.
Merge small tiles early so the board does not fill up.

title: Moon Rover: Anaxagoras
pitch: Drive a solar rover across a lunar crater: radar sweeps, drill samples and an outpost that went silent.
description: Moon Rover: Anaxagoras is our hosted, renamed copy of an open-source 3D lunar survey game by winch, used under the MIT licence. You drive the MU-7 rover out from its sled, power it with a fold-out solar array, look under the lunar soil with ground-penetrating radar and drill core samples to haul home. Five missions lead from a cold start to the outpost that stopped transmitting, and a field codex fills with what you find. Every texture and sound is generated in your browser; progress stays in localStorage on its own web address. No cookies, no account. It needs WebGL2 and is best on a desktop or laptop with a keyboard.
howToPlay: Each mission card lists a few objectives in the top-left. Mission 1 (Cold Start): press T to deploy the solar array, drive 120 m from the sled, then press G for a radar sweep. Later missions have you park on radar echoes, deploy the arm (R), aim it with W A S D and click to drill, carry samples back to the sled, lay relay beacons (B) to keep contact, and hold E at the old station to recover its logs. Watch power and hull: shadowed ground does not charge the array, and the sled recharges you and takes your samples. There is no score and no game over: if the hull gives out, the rover is winched back to the sled. Tab opens the field codex; Esc pauses.
controls: W A S D or the arrow keys to drive, mouse to look (click the game to lock the pointer), T solar array, G radar, R arm and click to drill, Esc pause. Touch: twin sticks and buttons.
controlsShort: W A S D or arrows drive, mouse looks; T array, G radar, R arm + click drill; Esc pauses
controlsKeyboard: W/S or ↑/↓ throttle and reverse · A/D or ←/→ steer · Space brake · mouse look (click the game to lock the pointer), wheel zoom · T solar array · G radar sweep · R arm (then W A S D aims, click drills) · B relay beacon · E hold to interact · F lamps · C camera · P photo mode (Q/Z up/down, Shift fast) · H hide HUD · Tab codex · Esc pause and release the pointer · X right the chassis after a rollover. K (save the frame as a PNG) does nothing inside our frame, because the frame blocks downloads.
controlsTouch: Twin sticks: DRIVE (left) and LOOK (right). Buttons: CAM, LAMP, ARRAY, HUD, SHOT, BRAKE on the left; SCAN, ARM, DRILL, RELAY on the right. SHOT (save a screenshot) does nothing inside our frame. We have not tested the touch controls on a real phone.
tips: Deploy the solar array (T) first: it is the first objective and keeps your power up.
Park before drilling: deploying the arm (R) holds the chassis still while you aim.
Head back to the sled to recharge and unload samples. The Sample Bay holds 6.
Turn the lamps on (F) in shadowed craters, and check the field codex (Tab) after each discovery.
If it stutters, lower RENDER QUALITY under SYSTEMS on the main menu. It starts at a level guessed for your device.

faq.a: Our hosted, renamed copy of an open-source 3D lunar rover survey game by winch: it is based on REGOLITH (MIT) by winch. It is used under the MIT licence and credited on this page; it is not an official version and is not endorsed by the author.

faq.q: Why is it called Moon Rover: Anaxagoras?
faq.a: We renamed our copy so that we do not use the original game's name as our own; the MIT licence allows changes like this. The title, title screen and other text in the game now say Moon Rover: Anaxagoras, and the main menu and this page say it is based on REGOLITH (MIT) by winch. Nothing else about the game changed.

faq.q: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a: It has twin-stick touch controls, but it is a heavy 3D game and we have not tested it on real phones, so we cannot say how well it runs there. It is best on a desktop or laptop with a keyboard.

faq.q: What do I need to run it?
faq.a: A browser with WebGL2. The game has no fallback: without WebGL2 it may not start at all.
Yes. Progress and settings are kept in localStorage on the game's own web address (regolith.anaxagoras.v1 and regolith.anaxagoras.v1.set), in your browser only. There are no cookies and no account.
